title: AI ethics principles as governance baseline
text: Use the national AI ethics principles to structure responsible AI design and deployment. Translate principles into operational controls: documentation, oversight, monitoring, and accountability owners. Treat this as a governance scaffold that supports explainable decisions.

title: Privacy protection as a design constraint
text: Design AI systems to protect privacy and reduce the chance of unauthorized disclosure. For LLM chatbots, restrict what is collected, logged, and retained; apply redaction and role-based access. Document privacy decisions as part of the decision trace.

title: Transparency and explainability principle
text: Provide transparency about AI use and reasons behind outputs where feasible and appropriate. Operationalize this via user notices, operator guidance, and documentation of limitations and uncertainty. Explainability is not just a UI message; it is a governance capability.

title: Accountability for AI outcomes
text: Organizations remain accountable for AI outcomes even when using third-party models. Assign accountable owners, define escalation paths, and maintain decision logs for exceptions. This ensures incidents produce explainable accountability rather than confusion.

title: APP 11: security of personal information
text: Take reasonable steps to protect personal information from misuse, interference, loss, and unauthorized access/disclosure. For AI systems, treat conversation logs and derived artifacts (embeddings) as personal information when they can relate to an individual. Maintain controls and evidence of implementation.

title: APP 11: retention and destruction/de-identification
text: Actively consider whether retention is permitted and destroy or de-identify personal information when no longer needed. For LLM applications, define retention windows for raw logs vs aggregated metrics. Evidence should include retention policy + enforcement mechanism.

title: Reliability and safety principle (test + monitor)
text: Define reliability expectations, test the system, and monitor performance in operation. For chatbots, focus on failure modes like hallucinations, harmful content, and unsafe advice. Tie monitoring signals to incident response and improvement actions.

title: Human oversight for high-impact scenarios
text: Keep humans central and implement oversight for higher-impact decisions or harm scenarios. Define when humans review outputs, when the system must escalate, and how overrides are logged. Oversight must be operationally feasible and trained.

title: Access restrictions for logs and personal data
text: Restrict access to personal data (including AI logs) using role-based access and auditing. Ensure privileged access is logged and periodically reviewed. This enables explainable accountability when investigating incidents or complaints.

title: Secure logging practices for personal information
text: If logs contain personal information, treat them as regulated: protect, restrict access, and manage retention. Apply redaction/minimization for sensitive fields and store only what supports security and accountability. Logging should be designed to be useful *and* privacy-preserving.
